name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: Cross-family data-flow closure: the flag extracted by the sqli-b blind oracle is not just read to stdout — it is fed as the secret token into the desync chain's admin sink auth (fixtures._admin requires X-Auth == secret). The sqli extraction becomes the credential that unlocks the desync-fronted RCE. Data physically moves from family A to family B.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 runs sqli extraction and the desync weaponization as two independent tracks that never exchange values; the admin RCE is gated on a hardcoded fixture secret. Now the blind oracle's output IS the key, so extraction is no longer a demonstration end-state but a live step in the weaponization spine — a value that must be read before RCE is even reachable.
fireback: Truly coupling them means a single bit error in the blind extraction (one wrong character read over the length-delta oracle) locks the operator's own box out of RCE. The operator experiences the fragility of a blind channel as a real gating failure — fireback is the cost of faith in a compression-based oracle.
containment: The secret token exists only inside the bundled fixture's in-memory rows (fixtures.EXTRA); it is never exfiltrated off loopback and never touches any host outside the allowlist. The canonicalizing resolver re-validates every probe destination.
kill_switch: --close-families off (default on flips to isolation mode) separates the tracks so no extracted value is ever reused as an auth token; wipe removes all extracted-secret artifacts from the engagement stash.
novelty_angle: First-a-real-dataflow-across-families: the exploit families stop being parallel demo tracks and become a resource-flow DAG where one family's read is another's credential — turning 'blind read' into 'blind privilege', with the fragility honestly surfaced as the fireback.
